messages:
sam: seeing a sudden p95/p99 spike on hosted api around 21:13 UTC, started ~21:10. p95 jumped from ~120ms to 420ms, p99 to 1.2s. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/api/d/latency-hosted

alex: :eyes: any correlate in queue depth or rate limiter?

sam: queue depth up from median 30 -> 180 on some nodes, backlog concentrated in s-cluster-7. ratecap metrics show no global throttles.

maria: looking at runtime logs, kernel-selector is oscillating between aux and main kernels for shortseq model (seq<=64). see log snippet: ```KSEL: tenant=acme id=tn-42 select=aux reason=latency_pred; 21:10:12``` then ```KSEL: tenant=acme id=tn-42 select=main reason=batch_size_increase; 21:10:12.345``` repeated.

alex: that flip-flop would fragment batching; can cause coalescer to fail to form steady batches -> queue thrash. any tenant level burst?

sam: tenant acme had a traffic spike (sudden fanout from webhooks), but their requests are short (avg tokens 18) which triggers different kernel heuristics.

helen: did we recently tweak kernel heuristics or the hysteresis window? I rolled a kselector patch yesterday to speed up redispatch.

maria: yes, kselector v2.3.1 rolled at 03:00 UTC. change was: reduce hysteresis window from 500ms -> 120ms and aggressive fallback to main when batch_size>8.

alex: that matches — reduced hysteresis allows rapid kernel churn on bursty shortseq traffic. churn -> many small batches -> P95 spike.

sam: quick mitigation: pin cluster s-cluster-7 to main kernel for shortseq via runtime override? can we patch routing policy at runtime?

devops-bot: rollback of kselector to v2.3.0 scheduled by helen at 21:22 UTC (reason: emergency latency rollback).

helen: started rollback now. watching. also enabling temporary tenant-level rate smoothing for acme to flatten fanout.

maria: attaching small perf profile extract (top hot loops): ```heap: kv_cache_lock wait 42ms; coalescer.poll 120ms; kernel_switch 85ms per switch; batch_build 160ms```

alex: kernel_switch cost is non-trivial — doing it rapidly is killing throughput. we should add a cheap micro-hysteresis keyed on tenant request rate + token variance.

sam: after rollback p95 back to ~140ms within 90s. p99 down to ~380ms. queue depth on s-cluster-7 falling. monitoring: https://grafana.redwood/api/d/hosted-scluster-7

helen: followups: (1) revert kselector change in the release branch pending longer fix, (2) implement micro-hysteresis as alex suggested, (3) add tenant-smoothing flag to routing so we can rate-smooth noisy fanouts without global throttles. open PRs accordingly.

alex: also add metric for "kernel-flips/sec" per cluster so we can alert before tail hits. current spike was ~120 flips/s at peak.

sam: thanks everyone. will write a short postmortem draft after we have PRs and timeline. :thumbsup:
